newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam approves tougher graft, drugs penalties.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam approves tougher graft, drugs penalties.

text.p: Vietnam's National Assembly has approved amendments to the criminal code that will bring stiffer penalties for corruption and drug-trafficking, state media reports said on Monday.

Under the new code, officials who take bribes worth 50 million dong ($4,290) or more will automatically be sentenced to death or life imprisonment. The same punishment will be handed out for the theft of public property worth 500 million dong or more.
Suspended sentences will be halted, a move that will send first-time graft offenders directly to jail.
Current laws on corruption are vague and stipulate that capital punishment should be reserved for serious cases of theft, misappropriation or embezzlement of "socialist property".

The graft provisions, approved by 85 percent of the legislature's deputies on Saturday after a week-long debate, are a signal of the communist government's new offensive against a scourge that pervades every level of society.

The drive against graft reached a high point earlier this year when four people were sentenced to death for siphoning off millions of dollars from Tamexco, a party-affiliated trading company in Ho Chi Minh City.

The Thoi Bao Kinh Te Viet Nam (Economic Times) said on Monday that 25 people suspected of involvement in corruption at the state-owned Nam Dinh textile company would stand trial at the end of this month. They are accused of losing $1.34 million of state money and pocketing around $124,400.

The Assembly also passed amendments to laws against opium poppy cultivation and heroin trafficking, which stipulate life in jail or the death sentence for possession of five kg (11 pounds) of opium or 100 grams (3.5 ounces) of heroin.
Previously, possession of one kg (2.2 pounds) or more of heroin was punishable by death.
The heavier penalties for drug trafficking came as a major drugs trial involving 22 people, half of them border guards or state police officials, was under way.

Captain Vu Xuan Truong, a lead defendant in the trial which opened on Friday, has vowed to expose some "extremely important people" during the hearing and the presiding judge has predicted that more than 10 people may be sentenced to death.
